description: Screenshot/OCR evaluation of the ClearCart text classifier on ContextRico-DP. ContextRico is used for evaluation only; no model is trained or tuned on it except the choice of OCR config and flagging threshold, which uses the DEV split only.

dataset.name: ContextRico-DP
dataset.filename_mapping: GT keys are bare filenames; each matches exactly one file under Mobile/ or Web/ (no duplicate basenames).
dataset.negatives_note: Negatives are ContextRico images with NO text-observable label. They are still dark-pattern UIs of visual types (Hard to Close, Nagging, Default Choice, False Hierarchy, ...) and some may contain unlabelled urgency/scarcity/social-proof or confirmshaming text, so the 'flag rate on negatives' (and hence image-level false positives / precision) is an UPPER bound on true false alarms.

split.rule: 50/50 DEV/TEST by image, seed 42; negatives and positives split separately, positives further stratified by their rarest ClearCart category

decision_rule: image is flagged for category c if any OCR candidate (line or merged block) has p_dark >= tau and top dark category c; flagged overall if any candidate has p_dark >= tau. Positive = image with >= 1 text-observable GT label. detection_recall = positives flagged with any category; category_correct_recall = positives flagged with >= 1 of their GT categories; precision/F1 use detection (any flag) on positives vs negatives, so they depend on the ~1:3 pos:neg ratio here.

v1_naive.description: raw RGB image, Tesseract auto layout (psm 3), one candidate per OCR line

v2.description: grayscale + 2x upscale (if max side < 2200px), sparse-text layout (psm 11), lines only

v3.description: v2 + adjacent lines of the same Tesseract paragraph also merged into block candidates

v4_psm3.description: grayscale + 2x upscale + block merging, but auto layout (psm 3)

selection_rules.joint_config_and_threshold: On DEV only, evaluate every (config, tau) with tau in {text-model threshold} U {0.3..0.9 step 0.05}. Admissible points have negative-image flag rate <= 0.15. Choose the admissible point with the highest image-level F1; points within 0.01 F1 of the best are tied and broken by higher category-correct recall, then by the text model's own threshold, then by lower OCR s/image. If an admissible point at the text model's own threshold is within 0.02 F1 of the best, it is preferred (no OCR-specific threshold unless it clearly helps). If no point is admissible, the lowest neg flag rate wins.

selection_rule_revision: The first run used a two-stage rule (pick the config by DEV F1 at the text model's threshold 0.68, then sweep tau for that config only). It selected v1_naive and then replaced 0.68 with 0.9 because 0.68 violated the neg-rate bound for every config - i.e. the config was chosen at a threshold that was then discarded. That run printed TEST metrics for v1_naive@0.68 and v1_naive@0.9 (cat-correct recall 0.634/0.512, F1 0.561/0.597) before the rule was replaced by the joint rule above, which was fixed after looking only at DEV sweeps. No other TEST numbers were seen before the revision. Both are reported here; test.all_configs_at_tau_0.9 lets a reader check every config.

chosen.reason: 4 of 56 DEV (config, tau) points meet neg flag rate <= 0.15; best admissible F1 0.7447. Chosen v4_psm3@0.9: F1 0.7447, cat-correct recall 0.8333, neg flag rate 0.136. Tie set: ['v4_psm3@0.9']. No admissible point at the text model's threshold.

error_analysis_test_chosen.reason_method: auto_reason is a heuristic: category confusion if any other category was flagged; otherwise it checks whether category cue words (regex, used only for this description) appear in the OCR text and the mean Tesseract word confidence (< 0.6 => 'garbled').

caveats: Negatives are ContextRico images with NO text-observable label. They are still dark-pattern UIs of visual types (Hard to Close, Nagging, Default Choice, False Hierarchy, ...) and some may contain unlabelled urgency/scarcity/social-proof or confirmshaming text, so the 'flag rate on negatives' (and hence image-level false positives / precision) is an UPPER bound on true false alarms.
Small positive sets (DEV 42, TEST 41 images; social proof has only 11 images in total) - see the Wilson CIs and paired McNemar p-values before reading much into differences.
OCR timings are wall-clock per call with 6 concurrent Tesseract processes (cached on first run); compare them relative to each other.
The backend Auditor suppresses a flagged block that lies inside an already-flagged line; for image-level 'any flag' this is equivalent to the rule used here, but per-category it can differ slightly.

runtime_seconds.note: a cold run (empty OCR cache, 1332 OCR jobs) took 174.6 s total / 156 s OCR; see screenshot_eval.log
